covers: route_start: a rating goes to follow_up, the only station that can log it
checkin_log: a rating finds the check-in row that is waiting for it

The drafted opening is 52 characters, so the shortcut did not fire: the turn landed in `ask`, which has no log_checkin, and the model reached for discuss_idea -- it read a verdict on something already tried as a new idea to debate. It recovered two turns later and the rating reached the waiting row. The seeded row is the state a real second conversation is in: the check-in was logged last time and the rating was not. An error analysis of all 41 failing full-agent case-runs found the cause is shared, not this case's: the agent recognises only three kinds of message in code before routing -- a button, a short rejection, a short rating with a row waiting -- and routes everything else by where the conversation is, not by what the message says. The same cause accounts for 26 of the 41 failures, across cases 27, 34, 35, 41, 43 and 44. Named as a known limitation of v1.0.0; the fix -- understanding a message before routing it -- is planned for v1.1, and this case moves back to regression when it passes.
